newsitem.title: GERMANY: German ministers to forgo 1997 pay rise.
newsitem.headline: German ministers to forgo 1997 pay rise.

text.p: The German government, practising what Chancellor Helmut Kohl preaches, will not take a pay rise this year, a cabinet minister said on Friday.

"The government has decided to forego a pay rise this year once again," Chancellery Minister Friedrich Bohl told RTL television, adding this was the fourth time in the last five years the government had taken such a decision.

Kohl provoked the ire of trade union leaders earlier this week when he suggested in a newspaper interview that Germans should accept little or no real wage increases over the next few years in a bid to create jobs.
"I believe this is a good, correct and visible sign that we are addressing this appeal to ourselves and that we are taking the need to make savings seriously," Bohl said.

Kohl's government is under pressure to cut Germany's jobless figure -- which has reached a post-war high of 4.66 million -- while meeting the strict Masstricht public spending targets to qualify for Europe's planned economic and monetary union.
